Option B is a tricky distractor that frames a coach-chosen tactic ('increasing visibility') as an open question—disguised advice offered before exploring the limiting belief. Option C is a tricky distractor that mimics challenging assumptions, yet uses cross-examination ('ask for factual proof') that can provoke defensiveness rather than curiosity.

mock_exam_batch.competency_reference: Core Competency 7: Evokes Awareness
mock_exam_batch.scenario_question: A client says, "I feel stuck behind a glass wall where everyone sees me working, yet nobody hears me." What is the BEST response for the coach?

options.text: Invite the client to unpack what that glass wall metaphor represents right now.
Ask what specific meeting the client could schedule this week so leaders hear their ideas.
Suggest sending brief weekly progress summaries to senior leaders so the client's work stands out.
Ask why colleagues and senior leaders tend to overlook the client's input during group discussions.

ai_rationale.explanation: Option A is correct under 2025 ICF Core Competency 7 (Evokes Awareness), which encourages using the client's own metaphor to deepen insight and generate new awareness before moving to action. Staying inside the glass wall image allows rich exploration of the client's experience without coach assumptions. Option C is clearly wrong because recommending weekly summaries replaces inquiry with direct advice. Option B is a tricky distractor that uses an action-oriented question, yet jumps prematurely into Competency 8 tactics (and implies scheduling a meeting) while bypassing the rich metaphor. Option D is a tricky distractor that sounds curious, yet abandons the metaphor, centers third-party motives, and asks a speculative 'why' question.

mock_exam_batch.competency_reference: Core Competency 1: Demonstrates Ethical Practice — Coaching vs. Consulting
mock_exam_batch.scenario_question: A client holds two competing job offers and asks the coach to evaluate both compensation packages and pick the smarter move. What is the BEST response for the coach?

options.text: Review both compensation packages closely and recommend whichever offer gives stronger long-term financial upside.
Analyze the financial strengths and drawbacks of both packages while letting the client decide.
Explain that advising on offers lies outside coaching and explore which decision criteria matter.
Clarify that evaluating offers is outside coaching and refer the client to career counselors.

ai_rationale.explanation: Option C is correct under 2025 ICF Core Competency 1 (Demonstrates Ethical Practice — Coaching vs. Consulting) and Competency 8 (Facilitates Client Growth). Evaluating compensation packages and selecting the best offer belongs to consulting or financial advising and compromises client autonomy; explaining that boundary while exploring the client's own decision criteria keeps the work purely coaching. Option A is clearly wrong because evaluating and choosing an offer directly breaches the Coaching vs. Consulting boundary. Option B is a tricky distractor because letting the client make the final pick sounds client-led, yet performing expert financial evaluation still casts the coach as a consultant. Option D is a tricky distractor representing rigid over-correction: clarifying scope does not require referring out when a coach can still partner on the client's own career criteria.

mock_exam_batch.competency_reference: Core Competency 7: Evokes Awareness
mock_exam_batch.scenario_question: Mid-session, a client suddenly says, "Wait — I've been blaming my director when I actually never stated my boundaries clearly." What is the BEST response for the coach?

options.text: Reassure the client not to be hard on themselves because directors rarely ask anyway.
Acknowledge that sudden realization and ask what opens up for them with this awareness.
Explore which exact boundary the client will state to their director this week.
Ask why the client avoided stating their boundaries clearly with the director for so long.

ai_rationale.explanation: Option B is correct under 2025 ICF Core Competency 7 (Evokes Awareness). When a client voices a fresh breakthrough in self-awareness, acknowledging the moment and asking what opens up helps the client deepen and integrate the insight before moving to action. Option A is clearly wrong because reassuring the client and faulting the director rescues them from owning their meaningful realization. Option C is a tricky distractor that uses exploratory phrasing ('explore'), yet rushes straight into Competency 8 action planning before allowing the client to unpack the breakthrough. Option D is a tricky distractor that uses an investigative question, yet shifts backward into 'why' justification and self-criticism rather than forward-looking awareness.

mock_exam_batch.competency_reference: Core Competency 8: Facilitates Client Growth
mock_exam_batch.scenario_question: A client commits to holding a difficult peer conversation by Tuesday, yet lowers their voice and looks hesitant. What is the BEST response for the coach?

options.text: Confirm Tuesday as their firm deadline and ask how they will report progress afterward.
Note that the client sounds fearful and suggest sending a brief written message instead.
Offer to role-play the difficult conversation now so the client feels prepared by Tuesday.
Note their quieter tone neutrally to explore what surrounds Tuesday's commitment right now.

ai_rationale.explanation: Option D is correct under 2025 ICF Core Competency 8 (Facilitates Client Growth) paired with Competency 6 (Listens Actively). Partnering around genuine client-owned action and self-accountability means noticing verbal hesitation neutrally and exploring what surrounds the commitment so the client can adjust or truly own the plan. Option A is clearly wrong because locking in accountability while ignoring clear hesitation risks setting an unaligned commitment. Option B is a tricky distractor that sounds considerate, yet labels the client's emotion ('fearful') and prescribes an easier alternative ('written message'). Option C is a tricky distractor that offers helpful rehearsal, yet rushes to rescue or prepare the client before checking whether Tuesday's commitment actually fits.

mock_exam_batch.competency_reference: Core Competency 8: Facilitates Client Growth
mock_exam_batch.scenario_question: A client opens Session 4 excitedly reporting they completed every action step committed to last week. What is the BEST response for the coach?

options.text: Celebrate their progress and ask what they learned about themselves through those actions.
Congratulate them briefly and ask what bigger steps they want to commit to next.
Ask them to walk step by step through how they completed every task.
Highlight how effectively coaching is working and assign more ambitious goals for next week.

ai_rationale.explanation: Option A is correct under 2025 ICF Core Competency 8 (Facilitates Client Growth), which highlights celebrating client progress and partnering to harvest learning from completed actions so growth becomes sustainable. Option D is clearly wrong because the coach claims credit for the outcome and assigns goals unilaterally, undermining client autonomy. Option B is a tricky distractor that sounds encouraging and forward-moving, yet skims past progress and rushes immediately into setting larger tasks before capturing what made the client successful. Option C is a tricky distractor that sounds interested in the client's actions, yet shifts the session into a detailed status audit rather than celebrating growth and evoking self-awareness.

mock_exam_batch.competency_reference: Core Competency 8: Facilitates Client Growth
mock_exam_batch.scenario_question: Approaching the final session of a six-month engagement, a client asks how to maintain momentum after coaching ends. What is the BEST action for the coach?

options.text: Propose renewing the coaching contract for another six months to protect their recent momentum.
Provide a proven post-coaching checklist of weekly habits for the client to follow afterward.
Partner to design lasting self-support practices by reviewing what worked well together.
Ask the client to lock in five new quarterly goals before the final session.

ai_rationale.explanation: Option C is correct under 2025 ICF Core Competency 8 (Facilitates Client Growth, specifically Sub-competency 8.07: partnering with the client to close the engagement in a way that respects the client and the coaching experience). Reviewing what worked well and partnering to design client-owned sustainability practices honors respectful closure and client autonomy. Option A is clearly wrong because pitching a contract renewal fosters dependency rather than supporting autonomous closure. Option B is a tricky distractor that seems helpful and structured, yet substitutes a coach-authored checklist for client-designed ownership. Option D is a tricky distractor that sounds goal-focused, yet pushes heavy task quotas instead of facilitating reflective closure and sustainable self-support.
